text: Thanks for making the time today. Before we talk about Salesforce at all - walk me through what happens when a new lead comes in. Who touches it first, and where does it usually get stuck?
So today that lives in a spreadsheet, and the handoff to sales is a Slack message that sometimes gets missed. That's the pain: leads go quiet because nobody owns the follow-up. Did I get that right?
Two ways to build that. A Flow-based assignment with an escalation timer gets you live in about a week. Custom Apex routing scales past fifty thousand records a month but costs more to maintain.
Given your volume, I'd start with Flow and design the data model so Apex can take over later without a migration. The one risk it carries: Flow debugging is weaker, so we add logging from day one.
So the readback: must-have is that no lead sits unowned for more than an hour. Nice-to-have is the manager dashboard. Anything I missed before we score your current org against that?
And while we were talking, the assessment already started. When we come back, you'll see your org's score and the three things dragging it - not a proposal, the actual findings.
